package_info.why_malicious: The affected Struts2 versions contain a critical deserialization vulnerability in the REST plugin's XML handling, allowing attackers to submit crafted XML payloads that result in remote code execution (RCE) on the server. This enables attackers to take full control of vulnerable systems remotely.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when REST endpoint receives XML payload)
execution_context.file_location: Struts2 REST plugin (uses XStream for XML deserialization)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: This XML payload, when submitted to a vulnerable Struts2 REST endpoint, is deserialized by XStream into a Java ProcessBuilder object, which then executes arbitrary system commands on the server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code allows arbitrary object instantiation and method invocation via user-supplied XML, enabling attackers to execute system commands.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal REST API XML input should only represent simple data structures, not executable code or system-level objects.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate use would only deserialize whitelisted, safe data types (e.g., DTOs, POJOs) and never allow arbitrary class instantiation.
key_indicators: Deserialization of user-supplied XML into arbitrary Java objects
Presence of ProcessBuilder or Runtime classes in XML payload
No input validation or type restriction on deserialized objects

attack_chain.action: Attacker crafts malicious XML payload containing Java objects (e.g., ProcessBuilder) to execute system commands.
attack_chain.leads_to: Payload is sent to vulnerable Struts2 REST endpoint.

attack_chain.action: Struts2 REST plugin receives and deserializes the XML using XStream, instantiating attacker-controlled objects.
attack_chain.leads_to: Arbitrary code execution on the server (RCE).

attack_chain.action: Attacker gains remote control of the server, potentially exfiltrating data or deploying further malware.

behavioral_signatures: Deserialization of untrusted XML input via XStream
Unexpected instantiation of ProcessBuilder, Runtime, or similar classes from REST API input
Execution of system commands triggered by REST API requests
file_indicators: XStream library present in application dependencies
network_indicators: Unusual POST requests with XML payloads to REST endpoints
Outbound connections initiated by the application server after receiving XML input
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for REST API endpoints that accept XML input and check for deserialization of untrusted data. Look for instantiation of dangerous classes (e.g., ProcessBuilder) in application logs or via runtime instrumentation. Use application firewalls to block suspicious XML payloads and scan dependencies for vulnerable Struts2/XStream versions.
